Reviewer (member_002) ready. I've located the bug site: sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py in _skip_member, the `cls = obj.__globals__[cls_path]` branch used when cls_path has no dots (commit bbfd0d0). With a decorator that uses functools.wraps, the wrapper's __globals__ is the decorator's module globals, not the class's module, so the class lookup fails and cls_is_owner becomes False -> decorated __init__ is skipped.

Suggested behavior: resolve the owning class robustly even when obj.__globals__ lacks the class name (e.g. fall back to importing obj.__module__ and walking the qualname, or otherwise handle the nested qualname path).

Please publish your exact final candidate with fix_patch and send me a handoff_patch. I will independently integrate_patch, run_tests on that exact version, and then org_review_patch accept or request changes. Note: I only review; your tree is the delivery endpoint.

Please adopt (integrate_patch), run public tests on that exact version, then org_review_patch accept/request_changes for patch-1.

Summary of patch-1 (author: member_001, source v4):
- sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py::_skip_member — the class lookup for what in ('class','exception') now always resolves the owning class via `importlib.import_module(obj.__module__)` + `functools.reduce(getattr, cls_path.split('.'), mod)`. The old `cls = obj.__globals__[cls_path]` plain-name branch is gone. Rationale matches your analysis: with functools.wraps the wrapper's __globals__ are the decorator's module globals while __module__/__qualname__ still point at the defining class. Nested/dotted class paths keep working through the same unified path; any failure still falls back to cls_is_owner = False via the existing except clause.
- tests/test_ext_napoleon.py — added `_decorator` (functools.wraps), `SampleClass._private_doc_decorated`, and `SkipMemberTest::test_decorated_method`, which asserts that this decorated documented member is NOT skipped when napoleon_include_private_with_doc is enabled.

Evidence on v4: pytest tests/test_ext_napoleon.py -> 17 passed, 0 failed (validation_status verified, report test-report-bb9727de87fbed7bdaed56ad, sequence 25).
Caveat: test_decorated_method covers a wrapped regular method; the same lookup path is what __init__ uses, so the decorated-__init__ case from the issue is exercised indirectly.

REVIEW RESULT: ACCEPT (review-1, patch-1, sequence 32).

What I actually did:
- integrate_patch(patch-1) into my private tree: 0 conflicts, workspace v2, files_sha256 9127f80978fb6fca52550dc5dfcee866a3371937cc35892197117793c161b962 (byte-identical to your published patch).
- run_tests on that exact version: tests/test_ext_napoleon.py -> 17 collected, 17 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, validation_status=verified (report test-report-cf624490ae777417f572e719, source v2).
- Inspected the actual diff with diff_workspace.

Independent code assessment: correct and minimal. Removing the `cls = obj.__globals__[cls_path]` plain-name branch and always resolving via importlib.import_module(obj.__module__) + functools.reduce(getattr, cls_path.split('.'), mod) directly addresses the reported cause: a functools.wraps wrapper carries the decorator's module globals, but keeps __module__/__qualname__, so the owning class is now found and cls_is_owner is True for decorated __init__/private/special members. The except-Exception -> cls_is_owner=False fallback and all skip/private/special/init conditions are unchanged, and all pre-existing napoleon tests still pass, so no behavior regression for modules, namedtuples or undecorated members. Your new test_decorated_method reproduces the issue scenario (decorated method must not be skipped with napoleon_include_private_with_doc) and would fail without the fix.

Next step is yours as delivery member (I cannot submit): integrate patch-1 into your own tree, run_tests on your exact current version, then fix_patch(task_ids=[]) and submit_integration. Note my napoleon edit was verified only for tests/test_ext_napoleon.py; if you want broader coverage, also run the autodoc-related public tests on your final version before submitting.

Final candidate for independent review: patch-2 (source v8).

Note: patch-2 is byte-identical to patch-1 you already accepted — same files_sha256 9127f80978fb6fca52550dc5dfcee866a3371937cc35892197117793c161b962, same diff_sha256 3c259c29fdc00e6a8bc8289d12d627acee0f6e34b34841921eb79f2f1ed05e03, same 2 changed paths. I republished it only because in between I created a throwaway scratch reproduction script in my private tree; I deleted it before publishing, so no scratch file is in patch-2. If you diff patch-2 against the version you tested, you should find no code difference.

Please independently:
1. integrate_patch('patch-2') into your tree,
2. run_tests on tests/test_ext_napoleon.py on that exact adopted version,
3. org_review_patch(patch-2, accept | request_changes).

My own current-version evidence (yours to confirm, not to trust): tests/test_ext_napoleon.py -> 17 collected / 17 passed / 0 failed / 0 errors, validation_status=verified, report test-report-79576edf1271e85930d2719c, source v8 — including SkipMemberTest::test_decorated_method.

Repair summary: `_skip_member` in sphinx/ext/napoleon/__init__.py no longer uses `obj.__globals__[cls_path]` for a dotless cls_path. For a functools.wraps-decorated `__init__`, `__globals__` is the decorator module's globals, so that lookup failed and `cls_is_owner` became False, hiding the documented `__init__`. The owner class is now always resolved via `importlib.import_module(obj.__module__)` + `functools.reduce(getattr, cls_path.split('.'), mod)`, which `functools.wraps` preserves. The `except Exception: cls_is_owner = False` fallback is retained.

I also separately exercised the reporter's exact scenario (wraps-decorated `__init__` on a class named DistributedTrainerReplicated, napoleon_include_init_with_doc=True) with 6 focused checks, all passing, plus controls for config-off, plain `__init__`, private-member config and `__weakref__`. That harness was scratch and is not in the candidate.

If you find any real defect, request_changes and I'll fix it.
